title: Urbanization

source.name: Wikipedia — Urbanization
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: Urbanization (or urbanisation in British English) is the process by which human settlements are formed and become larger as more people live, recreate and work in cities and towns. It describes the population shift from rural to urban areas, the corresponding decrease in the proportion of people living in rural areas, and the ways in which societies and culture adapt to this change.

Urbanization is not merely a modern phenomenon, but a rapid and historic transformation of human social roots on a global scale, whereby predominantly rural culture is being rapidly replaced by predominantly urban culture. The first major change in settlement patterns was the accumulation of hunter-gatherers into villages many thousands of years ago. Village culture is characterized by common bloodlines, intimate relationships, and communal behaviour, whereas urban culture is characterized by distant bloodlines, unfamiliar relations, and competitive behaviour. This unprecedented movement of people is forecast to continue and intensify during the next few decades, mushrooming cities to sizes unthinkable only a century ago. As a result, the world urban population growth curve has up till recently followed a quadratic-hyperbolic pattern.

From the development of the earliest cities in Indus Valley Civilization, Mesopotamia and Egypt until the 18th century, an equilibrium existed between the vast majority of the population who were engaged in subsistence agriculture in a rural context, and small centres of populations in the towns where economic activity consisted only of trade at markets and manufactures on a small scale. Due to the primitive and relatively stagnant state of agriculture throughout this period, the ratio of rural to urban population remained at a fixed equilibrium. However, a significant increase in the percentage of the global urban population can be traced in the 1st millennium BCE.

With the onset of the British Agricultural Revolution and Industrial Revolution in the late 18th century, this relationship was finally broken and an unprecedented growth in urban population took place over the course of the 19th century, both through continued migration from the countryside and due to the tremendous demographic expansion that occurred at that time. In England and Wales, the proportion of the population living in cities with more than 20,000 people jumped from 17% in 1801 to 54% in 1891. Moreover, and adopting a broader definition of urbanization, while the urbanized population in England and Wales represented 72% of the total in 1891, for other countries the figure was 37% in France, 41% in Prussia and 28% in the United States.

Urbanization occurs either organically or planned as a result of individual, collective and state action. Living in a city can be culturally and economically beneficial since it can provide greater opportunities for access to the labour market, better education, housing, and safety conditions, and reduce the time and expense of commuting and transportation. Conditions like density, proximity, diversity, and marketplace competition are elements of an urban environment that are deemed beneficial. However, there are also harmful social phenomena that arise: alienation, stress, increased cost of living, and mass marginalization that are connected to an urban way of living. Suburbanization, which is happening in the cities of the largest developing countries, may be regarded as an attempt to balance these harmful aspects of urban life while still allowing access to a large extent of shared resources.

questions.q: How does the writer contrast village life with city life?
options: Villagers move house often, whereas city people usually stay in one place for life
Villagers are close and cooperative, while city people are strangers who compete
Villagers are very competitive, whereas city people tend to help one another
Villagers share a common language, whereas city people speak several languages
questions.explain: Đoạn 2: văn hóa làng – quan hệ huyết thống, thân thiết, cộng đồng; văn hóa đô thị – huyết thống xa, quan hệ xa lạ, cạnh tranh.

questions.q: Why did the balance between rural and urban populations stay fairly stable until the 18th century?
options: Towns were destroyed regularly by war and by serious diseases
People had no wish to leave the countryside to find new work
Farming was too undeveloped to allow a large share of people to live in towns
Governments strictly controlled the number of people living in towns
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: nông nghiệp “primitive and relatively stagnant” nên tỉ lệ nông thôn/thành thị giữ ở trạng thái cân bằng.

questions.q: What change took place after about 1800?
options: The rural population grew faster than the urban population
The urban population fell, as people returned to farm the land
City populations grew rapidly through migration and a population boom
The balance between town and country stayed exactly as before
questions.explain: Đoạn 4: Cách mạng Nông nghiệp và Công nghiệp phá vỡ cân bằng; dân số đô thị tăng chưa từng có do di cư từ nông thôn và bùng nổ dân số.

questions.q: What do the figures for 1891 in paragraph 4 show?
options: England and Wales were more urbanised than France, Prussia or the US
France was the most urbanised of the four countries listed
The United States had the largest urban population in the world
Prussia and France were as urbanised as England and Wales
questions.explain: Đoạn 4: năm 1891 tỉ lệ đô thị hóa của Anh và xứ Wales là 72%, so với 37% (Pháp), 41% (Phổ) và 28% (Mỹ).

questions.q: Which of the following is mentioned as a disadvantage of urban living?
options: A feeling of isolation and a higher cost of living
A smaller number of different jobs to choose from
Poorer access to education and to health services
A longer time spent travelling to and from work
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: những mặt hại gồm “alienation, stress, increased cost of living, and mass marginalization”.

questions.q: How does the writer present suburbanization in the final paragraph?
options: As a problem that gets worse as developing countries become wealthier
As a trend that is likely to replace big cities entirely in coming years
As a scheme that governments always organise carefully in advance
As one way to ease the drawbacks of city life while keeping shared resources
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: ngoại ô hóa “may be regarded as an attempt to balance these harmful aspects of urban life while still allowing access to a large extent of shared resources”.

questions.q: According to the text, cities can offer better access to jobs and education than rural areas.
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: sống ở thành phố có thể có “greater opportunities for access to the labour market, better education…”.

questions.q: The writer claims that urbanization began in the nineteenth century.
questions.explain: Đoạn 2–3: “not merely a modern phenomenon” – đã có từ khi con người tập trung thành làng và các thành phố đầu tiên ở Lưỡng Hà, Ai Cập, thung lũng Indus.
